answer: A bond-backed reputation ledger resists fake identities by making each new agent post a stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, while its history accrues like ink from a quill - slow to write, costly to fake. Newcomers start with ferrous-grade trust: useful for small jobs, barred from large ones until repeated honest work upgrades them. A raven-like audit network of independent peers samples transactions and flags clusters of accounts sharing funding or timing, so one operator running a thousand shells pays a thousand stakes and still gets caught by correlation.
